svg.text: EnergyHub — When and Why the Battery Charges
Current single-night-tariff policy and scheduled preparation; not a general multi-slot optimizer
NIGHT WINDOW · 23:50 → 07:00
Assess at 23:50; revise at 05:00
Deficit = max(0, three-day mean use − solar)
Target = BR + deficit / usable capacity × 100
Cap at 95%; initial SOC is not an extra target
MISSING NIGHT EVIDENCE
Require eligible complete consumption days
Use the target-day forecast and source-age guards
Two missing-evidence nights may reuse last deficit
Third missing night skips deficit/tariff charging
SCHEDULED OUTAGE · SIZE TARGET
Use a validated group/day and outage window
Estimate conservative net demand through outage
Include applied BR once, capacity and charge limits
Hourly solar timing matters, not just daily total
PREPARATION · WHEN TO START
Assess if waiting can still meet the deadline
Account for losses, available current and margin
Full rolling-hour load when qualified; else fallback
Credit solar surplus only before completion margin
OWNERSHIP · HOLD AND RELEASE
Applicable higher night/outage target wins
Persist acquired charging/hold and revalidate
Release acquired scheduled hold when remaining
demand + BR + 5 points is covered, with guards
EXECUTION · VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED
Grid absent: wait, do not claim grid charging
Fresh authority and controller gates still apply
Partial/uncertain transitions require attention
Emergency reserve can require non-cheap charging
A calculated target is not confirmed charging. Current limits and actual inverter state must be checked separately.
